The release ZIP contains no user files, so copy its app files over your installation without deleting your own data. ## Changes in v1.000.110 - **Multiplayer through Eden rooms (new, experimental).** ProsperoEden can join an Eden room, so a game's Local Wireless mode reaches other players over the internet: other PS5 consoles running ProsperoEden, and Eden on a PC. Open **Settings > Multiplayer**, join a room, then start the game and choose its Local Wireless mode. The home screen shows when a room is connected, the game overlay shows the delay to the room in milliseconds, and when the connection is lost the game closes and the launcher says why. See the [setup guide](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/main/docs/MULTIPLAYER.md). - **Private room.** Enter a room's address, UDP port, a nickname and its password. They are saved as you type them, and joining a public room does not replace them. Enter the room's IPv4 address: looking up a hostname does not work on the console yet. - **Public rooms.** A list of the rooms in Eden's public directory, with each room's game, how many players it has and whether it asks for a password. Rooms you can join come first, the busiest at the top; Left and Right move a page at a time and Triangle refreshes. Rooms that use another protocol version are marked and cannot be joined. - **For a stable multiplayer session**, everyone needs the same game and the same update of it, and the player who hosts the lobby should use 1x resolution with frame generation off. A host that cannot hold full speed ends the session for everyone. - **Connection problems are explained.** When a room cannot be joined, a panel says what happened and what to try: a wrong password, a full room, a room that did not answer, a name already in use. **Settings > Diagnostics** has the detailed log to send with a report. - **Self-update keeps the version it replaces.** After an update, the previous version's files stay in `/data/prosperoeden/previous-version/PPSA99008-backup` until the next update. See [Going back to the previous version](#going-back-to-the-previous-version). - **One place for your data.** Settings, saves and covers are only ever in `/data/prosperoeden`. When ProsperoEden could not get access to the console's storage at a start, it used to carry on with empty settings and no saves, which looked as if they had been lost; it now says so on the home screen and starts no game. Keys, firmware and games that an early version kept inside the app's folder are moved to `/data/prosperoeden` at the first start, so that replacing the app cannot remove them. - **120 Hz holds on a display with a variable refresh rate.** With **Refresh rate** at 120 Hz, such a display was read as not having switched and the output went back to 60 Hz. - **No more lost graphics device in shader-heavy scenes.** Long scenes could stop a game with `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`; draws are now handed to the GPU in smaller batches. Contributed by [Bauls Deep](https://github.com/bawsdeep). - **Eden updated** to its revision of 8 October (`67bada77`), together with the Vulkan driver (Mesa), its tools and the Payload SDK. - **The helper that gives ProsperoEden access to storage** no longer reads a title's kernel data after that title has exited during its start. ## Changes in v1.000.100 - **Frame generation (new).** Between two pictures a game draws, ProsperoEden can show one made up from them, so a 30 FPS game looks like 60. It is in **Settings > Video** and in each game's own settings, works with the Vulkan renderer, and needs your own copy of Lossless Scaling: without its `Lossless.dll` the settings are greyed out. See [Frame generation](#frame-generation). Contributed by [gyn7561](https://github.com/gyn7561). - **A new loading screen.** It lists the steps of a game's start (reading the game, starting graphics, building shaders, starting the game) with a progress bar; while shaders are built it counts them. A step that lasts gets its seconds shown, so a start that is stuck can be told from one that is slow. - **Cheats in a file of their own work.** A cheat file placed straight in a game's mods folder (`cheat_<name>.txt`) was listed and switched on, but changed nothing in the game. It does now. The session log also names the game's build ID, the name a cheat file for that version of the game has. - **A game no longer fails every start after a crash.** A crash, or a console that went down, could leave a game's shader cache file damaged; that game then crashed at every start on the same renderer. The damaged part is now cut off and the rest is kept. - **No more stutter from log writes.** Games dropped frames every few seconds while the logs were written. Logs are now written in the background once a second; **Settings > Diagnostics > Write logs at once** brings the old behaviour back, to find a crash. Contributed by [matschi95](https://github.com/matschi95). - **The FPS overlay with frame generation.** It shows the game's own rate (N) beside the rate on screen (F) while frames are being added, and its usual single figure otherwise. Contributed by [gyn7561](https://github.com/gyn7561). - **The log says why frame generation is not running**, in lines that start with `framegen:`. Contributed by [gyn7561](https://github.com/gyn7561). - **A Nix shell for building.** `shell.nix` sets up the whole build environment. Contributed by [Bauls Deep](https://github.com/bawsdeep). - **Issues are open on GitHub**, with forms for bug reports and game reports; they ask for the save data and the debug logs. See [Issues and reports](#issues-and-reports). ## Changes in v1.000.095 A bug fix for v1.000.090. If you are on v1.000.090, update. - **Stutter and crashes while playing are fixed.** In v1.000.090 every button press could make a game bring up its controller screen again: play stuttered, and some games crashed after a minute or two. A second, handheld controller was being connected beside the player's own at the first press. It is now only used when **Handheld** is the game's Controller type, or the only controller the game takes. ## Changes in v1.000.090 - **Download sources (new, early).** Games on a [RomM](https://github.com/rommapp/romm) server in your network appear in the Library and are downloaded to the console when you want to play them; see [Download sources](#download-sources). Contributed by [matschi95](https://github.com/matschi95). - **Save sync (new, early).** Each profile can keep its save data in step with a RomM server, synced before a game starts and after it ends, and paired by scanning a QR code; see [Save sync](#save-sync). Replaced save data is kept as a backup first. Contributed by [matschi95](https://github.com/matschi95). - **Controller type per game.** **Library > Game settings > Controls > Controller type** gives a game a Pro Controller, the Handheld controller, Dual Joy-Cons, a Left Joy-Con or a Right Joy-Con, for games that take a Pro Controller and then only work with another. - **Typing text.** When a game asks for text, the PS5's own on-screen keyboard opens, and what you enter goes to the game. - **Firmware 7.40 and 7.61: games no longer end at their first picture.** Contributed by [v0ltfault](https://github.com/v0ltfault). - **Game names without question marks.** A name with a look-alike character (a sequel's Roman numeral, full-width letters) is shown with plain letters, a name that is not text is skipped, and characters no font has are left out. - **System language in the start-up trace**, with the menu's language and the console fonts found, for reports from other consoles. - **Builds on GitHub.** Releases are now built by GitHub Actions from the tagged source. ## Changes in v1.000.080 - **Single Joy-Con games with the DualSense held as usual.** A game that has a single Joy-Con held sideways no longer needs the DualSense turned sideways: the stick, the four buttons and the motion sensors are turned to match, for each player. L1 and R1 stay SL and SR. - **What's new in the update dialog.** When an update is offered, **What's new** shows that release's notes before you decide. - **Start a game directly.** ProsperoEden takes `--rom <file>` and `--exit-after-game` as launch arguments, so a home screen forwarder can open one game; see [docs/FORWARDER.md](docs/FORWARDER.md). - **Filesystem access on firmware 13.60.** The bundled helper is updated with a fix for that firmware. - **Release ZIP opens with the right permissions.** Its files are stored open to all, as the console wants an app's files; unpacked with their permissions kept, they could give "Can't start the game or app" (CE-107750-0). ## Changes in v1.000.070 - **ProsperoEden starts wherever it is installed.** On a USB drive, extended storage, an etaHEN games folder or any other place ShadowMountPlus mounts it from, it could not find its own files and closed after a moment. It now reads its files from where the PS5 mounts the running app. - **Updates from the menu work on those installs too.** The update helper updates the folder ShadowMountPlus mounted the app from; an app installed as an image is not changed, and the dialog says to replace the image. - **Clearer error when the menu cannot start**, naming the file and the reason. - **Start-up trace for bug reports.** Each start-up step is written to the kernel log (`[ProsperoEden diag]`) and to `/data/prosperoeden/logs/boot-trace.txt`. ## Changes in v1.000.060 - **Updates from the menu.** When a newer release is listed on homebrew.page, ProsperoEden offers it each time it opens. **Update now** downloads and checks it, unpacks it beside the app, then closes so the update helper can replace its files; **Skip** keeps the current version until the next time it opens. Your saves, settings and own files in the app folder are kept. See [Updating](#updating). - **Lapy elevation included.** ProsperoEden carries its own one-shot helper built from upstream Lapy and sends it over the local ELF loader on port 9021; loading Lapy separately is no longer needed. - **The elevation helper no longer crashes when ProsperoEden starts.** Its start-up runs on one thread, and it is built from a corrected upstream release. ## Changes in v1.000.050 - **Profiles.** **Settings > Profiles** lists the people who play on the console, up to eight. Each profile keeps its own save data, its own settings (everything under Settings, and each game's own) and its own recently played games. See [Profiles](#profiles). If you update from an earlier version, your saves, settings and games played become the first profile's, with nothing to do. - **Button mapping.** Choose which DualSense button presses each of the game's buttons, for every controller, in **Settings > Controls**, or for one game in its settings. See [Button mapping](#button-mapping). - **Settings per game.** A game's settings now have Video, Performance, Audio, Controls and Language; each value follows Settings until you choose another. See [Settings per game](#settings-per-game). - **Performance settings.** **Settings > Performance** has seven switches that trade accuracy for speed, for every game or for one. See [Performance settings](#performance-settings). - **Cheats chosen one by one.** A mod that lists several cheats shows each under it with its own switch, and only the chosen ones run. See [Mods](#mods). - **Update notice.** When a newer release is listed on homebrew.page, the menu says so at the top right for ten seconds. Nothing is downloaded or installed. See [Updating](#updating). - **Leaving a game takes ten seconds at most.** If a game has not stopped ten seconds after Touchpad + L1, or after it ended by itself, ProsperoEden starts again and opens at the menu. Some games took minutes to close. - **Touchpad + L1 works while a game loads.** A load that hangs can be left; before, the only way out was closing ProsperoEden. - **A game's controller screen always gets an answer.** A game that takes only the handheld controller gets it in Docked mode too, and a game that names no controller gets a Pro Controller. Both used to leave the game waiting. - **Removed games leave the menu.** A game whose file leaves the game files folder leaves Continue Playing, Recently Played and the Library within two seconds, and is not started. - **Touchpad by its name.** The menu and this document say Touchpad + L1 and Touchpad + R1. - **The graphics driver's shader cache works again**, so shaders compiled in earlier sessions load when a game starts. - **A crash when a game with cheats stops is fixed.** - **Games start a little sooner**: the instruction decoder's tables are built from one reading of each pattern. - The graphics driver is built from Mihawk's current PS5 Mesa and Vulkan. ## Changes in v1.000.040 - **The launcher in your language.** It follows the language the PS5 is set to, in 29 languages. Arabic, Chinese, Greek, Japanese, Korean and Thai are drawn with the console's own fonts. Text that runs longer in another language makes its own room instead of being cut. - **Accessibility.** **Settings > Accessibility** adds **Larger text**, **High contrast** and **Reduce motion**. Warnings carry a mark as well as a colour. - **Save data in and out.** Import a game's save from a folder or from a Ryujinx data folder, and export a copy. See [Moving save data](#moving-save-data). - **A ten-second slowdown with the AMD FSR filter is fixed.** In a large open-world game, gameplay could start at 3-9 FPS for about ten seconds, and frames of about a tenth of a second kept coming afterwards. The texture cache was throwing away images the GPU had drawn, with a wait for the GPU each time, as soon as memory use passed a mark that the FSR filter's own images pushed it over. It now keeps them until graphics memory is really short. - **Smoother heavy scenes.** The renderer hands its work to the Vulkan worker in larger batches, and the emulated cores wait less on the GPU caches' locks. In the heaviest area of a test walk this removed drops to 26-28 FPS and cut the GPU thread's work by about a quarter. - **Touchpad as Minus in games.** A tap of the touchpad presses the game's Minus button, and a longer press holds it. The Touchpad + L1 and Touchpad + R1 shortcuts never reach the game as a press. - **A crash a few seconds into some games is fixed.** The motion sensors' updates could reach a part of the controller service that was not set up yet. - **Games' own system screens.** A game's error dialog, profile picker and similar screens use Eden's built-in versions, and its error dialog now answers the game instead of leaving it waiting. The firmware's versions could end a session with an out-of-memory error. - **More graphics memory.** The PS5 gives an app one pool of memory that the CPU and the GPU share, and ProsperoEden held about 3 GiB of it without using it: its heap took 3 GiB at start and the emulated console's page table 1 GiB. Both now take memory as they need it, which gives graphics about 2.6 GiB more in the largest game tested. That game ran out of graphics memory while loading at 2x; it now runs at 2x with the AMD FSR filter at a steady 30 FPS, with about 2 GiB to spare. The texture cache also measures its memory use from what is really left of the pool, instead of a driver figure that counted every allocation twice. - **A clearer message when a game runs out of graphics memory.** If a game still needs more than there is at a high resolution, give it its own lower one: Triangle on it in the Library, then **Resolution**. - **Games that accept only single Joy-Cons** now get one, and L1 and R1 are its SL and SR buttons, which those games ask for on their controller screen. - **Mods.** A game's patches, replacement files and cheats load from `mods/<title ID>/` next to `roms/`, and the game's settings list them with a switch each. `.ips` and text `.pchtxt` patches, which the emulator core could not apply, now work. The Library has one switch per game for all of its mods. See [Mods](#mods). - **120 Hz output.** **Refresh rate** in **Settings > Video**, and in each game's settings, asks the display for 120 Hz while a game runs. A display that cannot show it stays at 60 Hz, and the menu always runs at 60 Hz. After a game at 120 Hz the menu takes about five seconds to come back while the display changes rate. - **Output resolution.** **Settings > Video** has a new **Output resolution** row: 1080p (as before), 1440p or 2160p. It is the size of the picture ProsperoEden puts out, for the menu and for games. Until now a game's picture was made at 1080p and enlarged, whatever its internal resolution; at 2160p the upscaling filter scales the game straight to a 4K picture. A larger picture needs more graphics memory. - **3x and 4x resolution.** The internal resolution now goes up to 4x. These need far more graphics memory than 2x; a game that runs out says so, and can be given its own lower resolution. - **Patches for more frames than the display shows.** A game patched to run faster than the output refreshes keeps its pace: the frames the display has no refresh for are left out. - **Crash reports.** If ProsperoEden stops because of an error, it writes `crash-<date>-<time>.txt` to `/data/prosperoeden/logs`, starts again and says on the home screen where the report is. That session's logs are kept beside it, and the five newest reports stay. A report holds what failed, where in the app's code, and what was running; it never holds the contents of memory. - The launcher and the OpenGL renderer use the PS5 OpenGL 4.6 SDK 1.0.0. - The graphics driver's shader cache moved to `/data/prosperoeden/cache`, so a read-only package install keeps it. - **Experimental: block list.** With an empty file named `block-list.txt` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008`, ProsperoEden saves which code a 64-bit game compiled and compiles it again on a spare CPU when the game next starts. In a repeat session of a large open-world game, the emulated cores then compiled 426 blocks during play instead of 138,262, and gameplay started at 30 FPS instead of 22. It is off by default until more games have run with it. ## Changes in v1.000.030 - **New launcher.** Every screen is redrawn with OpenGL: smooth transitions between screens, text that stays sharp, panels that blur the artwork behind them, and sound effects for moving, selecting and going back. **Settings > Audio > Menu sounds** sets their level. - **Controllers on the home screen.** Four controller icons show which controllers are connected, and change as one joins or leaves. - **Loading screen.** An animated scene shows while a game starts, on both renderers. - **The Library opens at once.** The game list is read in the background, and the home screen shows each game's own name instead of its file name. - **New music** on the PS5 home screen. - **Smoother first-time gameplay.** The emulated CPU cores now share the code they compile, so each part of a game is compiled once instead of once per core. In large open-world games this halves the compile work and removes most of the stutter when gameplay starts or a new area loads. - **Faster compiling.** Compiling a game's code now takes about 40% less CPU time, which shortens the remaining stutter when gameplay starts or a new area loads. - **Startup hang fixed.** A game could stop for good right after starting, because the emulator's memory allocator could leave high-priority threads waiting on each other forever. Development builds also report where a slow start is stuck. - **Games close in about a second.** Touchpad + L1 used to take 10-25 seconds to return to the library; logging no longer waits on the console's storage, and the emulator skips needless teardown work. - **Up to four controllers.** Each signed-in PS5 user's controller becomes the next player (player 1 is whoever launched the game); controllers can join or leave during a game, and games that ask for controllers connect every one in use. - The Touchpad + L1 and Touchpad + R1 shortcuts work from any controller. - **Vibration and motion.** DualSense rumble for games that use it (turn it off in **Settings > Controls**), and the controller's gyro and accelerometer for motion controls. - **Resolution and upscaling.** **Settings > Video** now sets the internal rendering resolution (0.5x to 2x) and the filter that scales it to the TV: Bilinear, AMD FSR, Bicubic or Nearest. - **Per-game settings.** Press Triangle on a game in the Library to give it its own renderer, resolution and upscaling filter. - **Language setting.** **Settings > Language** picks the language games use (18 languages), with the console region that goes with it. It applies when a game starts. - **Game updates and DLC.** Put update and DLC files (NSP or XCI) in the `updates` folder next to `roms`; the newest update and all DLC apply when the game starts, and the game details show them. - **Build it yourself.** `make` fetches every dependency at its pinned revision and builds the release. The OpenGL renderer now uses the published PS5 OpenGL 4.6 SDK 0.6.0. ## Changes in v1.000.020 - **Vulkan is now the recommended and default renderer.** OpenGL remains available in Settings. - **Choose where your game files live.** The new **Settings > Game files** browser selects any folder, including external drives and USB devices. The old `assets/` folder keeps working until you choose one. - **App data moved to `/data/prosperoeden`.** Config, logs, covers, and saves now live outside the app folder, so updating the app never touches them. - **Settings are now stored in one JSON file.** Earlier text settings are migrated automatically on first launch. - **Faster Library navigation**, and covers and recent games that survive folder moves. - **New icons** for controller actions, pages, and the Handheld / Docked mode. **Known issues:** Ending a game with Touchpad + L1 can take several seconds. Some games can still hang on the loading screen, and some demanding games remain slow. This is a testing pre-release, not a compatibility guarantee. ## In-game shortcuts The touchpad is pressed as a button. On its own, a tap of the touchpad presses the game's Minus button (with the usual [button mapping](#button-mapping)), and a longer press holds it; a shortcut never reaches the game. | Shortcut | Action | |---|---| | Touchpad + R1 | Toggle the performance HUD | | Touchpad + L1 | End the running game and return to the library | ## Roadmap - **FPKG support** - install ProsperoEden as a fake package, alongside the current homebrew folder install. - **More performance** - CPU and GPU work to keep demanding games at their target frame rate: the short stutter when a game reaches new areas (the block list, **Compile ahead** in **Settings > Performance**, once it has run in more games and can be on by default), heavy cutscenes, and games that run slower in Docked mode than in Handheld. - **More reliable game loading** - a game that hangs while it loads can now be left with Touchpad + L1; the hangs themselves still need a log from a game that does it. - **Game names in the menu's language** - a game carries a name for each language; the Library shows the first one that is text. Show the one in the menu's language, and the name from an installed update when it has one. - **Real Joy-Cons and Pro Controllers (investigation)** - play with the original controllers connected to the PS5. The PS5 does not pair them itself, so this first needs to find out whether a homebrew app can read them: a wired Pro Controller over USB looks more likely than Joy-Cons, which only connect over Bluetooth. - **Keyboard as a controller** - map a USB keyboard's keys to the game's buttons, like the DualSense's. Text entry itself is done: it uses the PS5's on-screen keyboard. - **Multiplayer with Eden on other systems (investigation)** - join Eden's multiplayer rooms from the PS5 and play with Eden players on PC, Linux and Android, entering a room's address by hand, including a room hosted on your local network (no PSN needed). Rooms only accept the same Eden version on every side, so each release would name the matching PC version. - **DualShock 4 controllers** - use DualShock 4 controllers as players too, next to the DualSense, so multiplayer games do not need four DualSense controllers. - **Controller type for each player** - choose, for each of the four connected controllers, which controller the game sees: a Pro Controller, a pair of Joy-Cons, a single left or right Joy-Con, a GameCube controller, or Handheld mode, as Eden does on other systems. - **Better OpenGL performance** - make the OpenGL renderer faster, and add tuning options for it. - **More game compatibility** - validate more games on the PS5, and fix what keeps them from running well, such as games that crash at launch. ## Issues and reports Problems and ideas go to [GitHub issues](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/issues). Reports about a particular game are welcome: name the game, and say what happens and where. A report that can be acted on has: - the game and its version (and any update or mod in use); - the ProsperoEden version, the PS5 model and system software version, and what the console runs (kstuff-lite or etaHEN, ShadowMountPlus version); - the renderer, resolution and Performance switches; - the debug logs, attached as a ZIP: turn on **Settings > Diagnostics > Detailed logging**, make the problem happen again, then zip `/data/prosperoeden/logs` (after a crash, the crash report and the logs beside it); - for a problem at a certain spot in a game, your save data from just before it, attached as a ZIP: Triangle on the game in the Library, **Save data**, **Export a copy**, then zip the folder it writes in `/data/prosperoeden/save-export`. With it the spot can be reached without playing the game up to there. **No piracy.** ProsperoEden is for games you own and dumped yourself. Do not ask for, post or link to game files, keys or firmware, here or in any of the project's channels, and do not ask where to find them. Such posts are removed. ## Elevation credits Filesystem elevation uses [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon), created by ArkSama. ProsperoEden follows the cooperative owned-root design and implementation from [ProsperoEden's Lapy fork](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon), based on [mpereiraesaa's cooperative helper](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon). The build pins that source, builds its exact-title one-shot helper without local payload changes, verifies the upstream-generated manifest, and includes the resulting ELF in the release. The donor-release and firmware 13.60 fixes pinned here were merged upstream in [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon PR #48](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/48) and [PR #49](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/49). The pinned `57fcc19` helper also includes the guarded target-lifetime and fail-closed accounting changes from [PR #50](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/50). The previous `54a095c` helper passed five automated launch/elevate/close cycles on firmware 6.02 and five on 12.70 with root access and balanced donor references. The pinned helper completed the target-exit stress and a full one-shot elevation on firmware 12.70; it still requires an attended ProsperoEden qualification run on firmware 6.02. ## Thanks Thank you to the people who test ProsperoEden on their own consoles and report what they find: - **Jones** ([X](https://x.com/Jonesskulls), [GitHub](https://github.com/AgentJonesy)), for helping with testing. - **Phronesis**, for helping with testing. - **szampan** ([GitHub](https://github.com/heni0xyz)), for helping with testing. - **BunkinBacon**, for helping with testing. - **Cold** ([GitHub](https://github.com/JMUtechnologies)), for helping with testing. - **Bauls Deep** ([GitHub](https://github.com/bawsdeep)), for helping with testing. - **OverkillLabs**, for helping with testing. And to the people who contribute code: - **Mihawk** ([GitHub](https://github.com/mihawk-99)), besides the driver the Vulkan renderer runs on: cheats that can be chosen one by one, the fix for the crash when a game with cheats stops, the driver's shader cache working on the console, a fix for games that come without control data, and the driver build reading its versions from one place. - **quatrixone** ([GitHub](https://github.com/quatrixone)), for the Performance settings and their seven switches, also per game, and for a much faster first compilation of a game's code. - **Martin Pham** ([GitHub](https://github.com/MartinPham)), for starting a game straight from its path, which is what forwarders on the home screen use. - **matschi95** ([GitHub](https://github.com/matschi95)), for the RomM integration (browsing, downloading and playing games from your own server, and save sync) and for finding and fixing the stutter that log writes caused every few seconds. - **v0ltfault** ([GitHub](https://github.com/v0ltfault)), for tracking down why every game ended at its first picture on system software 7.40, with a fix and a write-up of the findings. - **gyn7561** ([GitHub](https://github.com/gyn7561)), for bringing frame generation to the PS5, with its settings, and for the log lines that say why it is or is not running. - **Bauls Deep** ([GitHub](https://github.com/bawsdeep)), for the Nix shell that sets up the whole build environment with one command. - **lunar-me** ([GitHub](https://github.com/lunar-me)), for a correction to the README. <!-- bbr-footer:start --> <!-- Generated by ps5-homebrew-dev-protocol/scripts/readme-footer. - **Multiplayer through Eden rooms (new, experimental).** ProsperoEden can join an Eden room, so a game's Local Wireless mode reaches other players over the internet: other PS5 consoles running ProsperoEden, and Eden on a PC. Open **Settings > Multiplayer**, join a room, then start the game and choose its Local Wireless mode. The home screen shows when a room is connected, the game overlay shows the delay to the room in milliseconds, and when the connection is lost the game closes and the launcher says why. See the [setup guide](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/main/docs/MULTIPLAYER.md).
- **Private room.** Enter a room's address, UDP port, a nickname and its password. They are saved as you type them, and joining a public room does not replace them. Enter the room's IPv4 address: looking up a hostname does not work on the console yet.
- **Public rooms.** A list of the rooms in Eden's public directory, with each room's game, how many players it has and whether it asks for a password. Rooms you can join come first, the busiest at the top; Left and Right move a page at a time and Triangle refreshes. Rooms that use another protocol version are marked and cannot be joined.
- **For a stable multiplayer session**, everyone needs the same game and the same update of it, and the player who hosts the lobby should use 1x resolution with frame generation off. A host that cannot hold full speed ends the session for everyone.
- **Connection problems are explained.** When a room cannot be joined, a panel says what happened and what to try: a wrong password, a full room, a room that did not answer, a name already in use. **Settings > Diagnostics** has the detailed log to send with a report.
- **Self-update keeps the version it replaces.** After an update, the previous version's files stay in `/data/prosperoeden/previous-version/PPSA99008-backup` until the next update. See [Going back to the previous version](#going-back-to-the-previous-version).
- **One place for your data.** Settings, saves and covers are only ever in `/data/prosperoeden`. When ProsperoEden could not get access to the console's storage at a start, it used to carry on with empty settings and no saves, which looked as if they had been lost; it now says so on the home screen and starts no game. Keys, firmware and games that an early version kept inside the app's folder are moved to `/data/prosperoeden` at the first start, so that replacing the app cannot remove them.
- **120 Hz holds on a display with a variable refresh rate.** With **Refresh rate** at 120 Hz, such a display was read as not having switched and the output went back to 60 Hz.
- **No more lost graphics device in shader-heavy scenes.** Long scenes could stop a game with `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`; draws are now handed to the GPU in smaller batches. Contributed by [Bauls Deep](https://github.com/bawsdeep).
- **Eden updated** to its revision of 8 October (`67bada77`), together with the Vulkan driver (Mesa), its tools and the Payload SDK.
- **The helper that gives ProsperoEden access to storage** no longer reads a title's kernel data after that title has exited during its start.

repos.readme:
Overdrive is a game store that runs on a jailbroken PS5. Browse the catalog, download with up to 64 connections at once, extract archives and hand finished games to ShadowMountPlus, all from the controller. This repository holds its builds. Install it once by hand; after that, Overdrive updates itself. > **Upgrading from the folder install?** It will stop getting updates soon. Follow > [MIGRATE.md](MIGRATE.md) to switch to the single-file image. ## What you need | | | | --- | --- | | **A jailbroken PS5** | Tested on firmware 13.60 | | **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** | Registers Overdrive and the games it downloads | | **An ELF loader on port 9021** | For example John Törnblom's elfldr. Overdrive uses it to install packages, and a folder install to reopen itself after an update | | **A way to copy files to the console** | FTP, [PS5Upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload) or a USB drive | ## Install 1. **Download** `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/half144/overdrive-releases/releases/latest). 2. **Unzip** it on your computer. You get a single file, `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`: the whole app in one exFAT image. 3. **Copy** that file to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (or to `homebrew/` on a USB drive plugged into it), so you end up with `/data/homebrew/Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`. Do not change its permissions: ShadowMountPlus mounts the image as it is. - **FTP:** connect to the console's FTP server and upload the file into `/data/homebrew/`. - **PS5Upload:** send the file with `/data/homebrew/` as the destination folder. - **USB:** copy the file to `homebrew/` at the root of an exFAT drive and plug it into the console. 4. **Register** it: with ShadowMountPlus running, Overdrive appears on the home screen within a few seconds. If it does not, run ShadowMountPlus's scan again. 5. **Open** Overdrive from the home screen. > Keep the file name `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`, and keep only one copy of Overdrive: if you had > the folder install, delete `/data/homebrew/PPSA99058` first so ShadowMount doesn't see two copies. > [MIGRATE.md](MIGRATE.md) walks through switching from the folder install.
Alternative: the folder install (deprecated) The folder install will stop getting updates soon; prefer the image above, or [switch to it](MIGRATE.md) if you already have the folder. 1. Download `Overdrive-PPSA99058.zip` from the latest release and extract it: you get a folder named `PPSA99058`. 2. Copy the whole folder to `/data/homebrew/`, so you end up with `/data/homebrew/PPSA99058/eboot.bin`. Keep the folder name: it is the title ID. 3. Set the folder's permissions to `777`, recursively. FTP clients such as zftpd write files as `0666`, which the console's loader refuses ("Cannot start the game or app"). 4. Register and open it as above.
## Updates Overdrive checks this repository a few seconds after it opens. When a newer release is out, it asks first: ``` UPDATE AVAILABLE v0.0.89 v0.0.88 → v0.0.89 [ Update now ] [ Later ] ``` **Update now** downloads the release, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for it, and installs it. An image install gets the new image in place of the old one: Overdrive then closes, and ShadowMountPlus mounts the new image when you open it again from the home screen after a few seconds. A folder install gets the new files swapped into its folder and reopens on its own. Your downloads, favorites and settings stay where they are. To update by hand instead, repeat the install steps over the existing file (or folder). ## Troubleshooting
"Cannot start the game or app" after copying the folder Only the folder install has this: the console's launcher needs to read every file in the folder. Set the folder's permissions to `777`, recursively (most FTP clients and PS5Upload can do it), then open Overdrive again. The image install never needs it.
Overdrive closes after an update but does not reopen With the image install that is expected: open Overdrive from the home screen. With the folder install, reopening needs the ELF loader on port 9021; without it the update still installs, and Overdrive runs the new version when you open it. If you reopen an image install too fast, the old version may open and offer the same update again: choose **Later**, close Overdrive and open it again after a few seconds. ShadowMountPlus releases the old image a moment after the app closes.
The update dialog never appears The console needs internet access to reach GitHub, and Overdrive only offers a release newer than the version shown next to its logo. GitHub allows 60 checks an hour per network; a busy shared connection can run out, and the next launch tries again.
Overdrive does not show up on the home screen Check that ShadowMountPlus is running and that the path is exactly `/data/homebrew/Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat` (or, for the folder install, `/data/homebrew/PPSA99058/eboot.bin`, not one folder deeper). If both the image and the `PPSA99058` folder are there, ShadowMountPlus sees the same title twice: delete the folder.
Every download fails with "No connection to the server" (or "Not enough free space" with plenty of room) The console can't resolve the download servers' names, so every download stops at 0 MB. Covers may still load, because Overdrive looks their addresses up on its own; downloads use the console's DNS. - **DNS set to `127.0.0.1`** (common with Y2JB and other jailbreak setups): that address is a DNS payload running on the console, such as NanoDNS. Load it before opening Overdrive, then choose **Retry**. - **Any other DNS**: set the console's DNS to `1.1.1.1` and `1.0.0.1` (or `8.8.8.8` and `8.8.4.4`) in **Settings > Network > Settings > Set Up Internet Connection**, then choose **Retry**. **Known bug, up to 0.0.106:** for games with "Space" in the name (Dead Space), a connection error is shown as "Not enough free space", and the download doesn't move on to the game's other sources. Your drive has room: fix the DNS as above and choose **Retry**. The next version fixes it.
## Releases Each release is tagged `vX.Y.Z` and carries two assets: - `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat.zip`: the app as a single exFAT image (64 KiB clusters, the app at the image's root). The recommended install. - `Overdrive-PPSA99058.zip`: the complete `PPSA99058` app folder, with mode `777` stored. Deprecated: it will be discontinued soon.

# PS5 File Manager

A desktop-style file manager for jailbroken PS5 consoles: movable windows,
tabs, a taskbar and a Start panel, driven by the controller.

Developed and tested on firmware 6.02. Other firmware versions are untested.

## Features

- Windows you can move, resize, snap side by side, minimise and merge as tabs
- Copy, move, rename, delete, with a recycle bin, undo, a job queue with
  pause, and a replace / skip / keep-both prompt on name clashes
- Read and write everywhere, including system partitions (deletes there are
  backed up to /data/ps5fm-backup)
- Video and music player with subtitles, audio tracks, speed control,
  frame step, resume, and saving a frame as a picture
- Picture viewer with zoom, rotate and slideshow
- Pictures, Videos and Music libraries scanned from every drive, with
  thumbnails
- ZIP create and extract; RAR, 7z, tar, tar.gz, xz and ISO extract
- Text editor and hex viewer
- Search across all drives, recent files, folder sizes, duplicate finder,
  folder compare and one-way sync, checksums, split and join
- Game names and icons in the app folders, save backup and restore to USB
- Six looks (Classic, Night glass, Graphite, Paper, Windows style,
  Mac style) plus a custom one, each in light and dark
- Home-screen tile; no web server needed

## Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port 9021
- A Linux PC with cmake, git, socat, make, python3 and nasm
- The ps5-payload-dev SDK in /opt/ps5-payload-sdk

## Build and install

    PS5_HOST=<console ip> ./build.sh run

The first build downloads and compiles SDL2, ffmpeg, zlib, xz and
libarchive into deps/, which takes several minutes. `./build.sh` alone
only builds; `./build.sh install` builds and installs without starting.

## Controls

| Control | Action |
|---|---|
| Left stick | Pointer |
| Right stick | Scroll |
| Cross | Click / open |
| Circle | Back / close |
| Square | Select; hold on a title bar to move, on an edge to resize |
| Triangle or R3 | Menu |
| L3 | Switch windows |
| L1 / R1 | Tabs, previous / next |
| Options | Exit |

## Warning

This app can modify and delete system files. Removing the wrong file can
stop the console from booting. Use it at your own risk.

## Licence

GPLv3. The launcher includes code from ps5-payload-dev/websrv (GPLv3).
The app links FFmpeg, libarchive, zlib, xz, SDL2, stb and miniz, each
under its own licence.

repos.readme: # LZ4 Game Compressor **Beta 2 — On-console PS5 game compression** LZ4 Game Compressor lets you compress your PS5 games directly on your console, helping reduce the space they occupy without having to transfer them to a PC or create a separate, fully extracted copy. It converts supported PS5 game sources into AMPR LZ4 asset packs, using ShadowMountPlus to mount game images when needed. Everything is managed through a browser-based interface that you can open on your PS5 or another device connected to the same local network. ## Supported sources **This app can only convert mountable PS5 game images and extracted PS5 game folder dumps.** Images must be mountable by ShadowMountPlus. A folder dump must contain the game's `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/param.json`, and game files. Images are read through their mounted files; the compressor does not extract the image format itself. Folder dumps are loaded through a read-only view. Already converted AMPR folders are excluded from the source library. ## Getting started ### What you'll need Before starting, make sure you have: - A homebrew-enabled PS5 - Payload Manager - ShadowMountPlus - A mountable game image supported by ShadowMountPlus, or an extracted PS5 game folder dump - Enough available storage for the converted game Keep ShadowMountPlus installed for image mounting and library refresh. Folder dumps do not need an image mount. ### Launching the compressor 1. Load `LZ4-Game-Compressor-beta.2.elf` using Payload Manager. 2. Open the compressor interface in your browser at: `http://:5911/` Replace `` with your console's local IP address. 3. Your game library should appear in the interface, ready for you to select a game. The same ELF installs or refreshes the app icon and **Media shortcut** on your PS5, so no separate shortcut installer is needed. You can also access the interface using that shortcut. Keep in mind that the shortcut only opens the interface; the compressor payload must already be running. ## Compressing a game The conversion process is designed to be straightforward, with most settings handled automatically. ### 1. Select your game Find the game you want to compress in your library. Each entry is labeled **Image** or **Folder Dump** and shows its drive and source path. Make sure no game is currently running. For an image, select **Mount game**. A folder dump loads automatically; the disabled button then reads **Folder Dump Loaded**. ### 2. Choose where to save it Select the internal SSD, an available M.2 expansion SSD, or a connected USB storage device as your conversion destination. An M.2 drive must already be recognized and mounted by the PS5. Custom folders such as `/mnt/ext1/homebrew` can be selected under **Destination folders**. You can customize the exact folder locations by expanding **Destination folders**. The compressor automatically checks whether your selected drives have enough free space before allowing the conversion to start. ### 3. Decide what happens to the original You can keep the original game, delete it after conversion, move it somewhere else, or exchange its location with the compressed version. If you're trying the compressor for the first time, **Keep both** is the safest choice. This lets you test the compressed game before deciding whether to remove the original. See [Managing your original games](#managing-your-original-games) for more information about each option. ### 4. Start the conversion Once everything is configured, select **Start conversion**. The compressor will take care of the required file copying, LZ4 compression, AMPR runtime installation, and game-readable permissions. You can follow the progress in real time, including conversion speed and estimated remaining time. These estimates reflect the steps selected for your particular conversion. If something needs attention before starting, the interface will explain what's missing beneath the Start conversion button. ### 5. Verify and finish **Content verification is enabled by default**, and it's recommended to leave it on. Verification checks the converted content for data integrity before the compressor performs any requested operations on the original game. You can skip verification, but the resulting game will be marked **Unverified**. A successful verification doesn't necessarily mean the game will launch or function correctly, so it's worth testing the converted game yourself. Once conversion finishes, your compressed game will be saved to the selected location. If you enabled **Restart ShadowMount after conversion**, the compressor will also restart ShadowMount to refresh its game library. ## Using the app from more than one device Open the same PS5 IP address and port on each device. Game selection, destination folders, compression level, verification choices, original-game options, and mount state stay synchronized between browsers. A conversion keeps running on the console when you close a browser. Opening the interface on another device shows the current stage, game, file, transfer speeds, elapsed time, estimated remaining time, and progress. Setup and Progress tab selection stays local to each browser. ## Managing your original games You don't necessarily have to keep two copies of every game. The compressor provides several options for organizing your storage after a successful conversion. | Option | What happens | |---|---| | **Keep both** | Your original game stays untouched, and the compressed game is saved to your chosen destination. | | **Delete original** | The original is permanently removed once the selected conversion checks have completed successfully. You'll be asked to confirm this choice. | | **Move original** | The original game is moved to another folder or drive after conversion. | | **Swap original and converted** | The compressed game takes the original game's place, while the original is relocated to the destination drive. | Folder dumps currently use **Keep both**. Moving, deleting, and swapping the original are available for image sources. ### Moving games between drives When moving an original game to another drive, the compressor copies and verifies it before removing the old file. This helps protect against data loss during transfers. The original game is unmounted before any operation that requires moving or deleting its image. ### Swapping game locations The **Swap original and converted** option is useful when you want the compressed version to remain on your main game drive while keeping the original on another drive. For example, you could compress a game from your internal SSD to a USB drive, then swap their locations so the compressed game ends up on the internal SSD and the original moves to USB. Swapping is only available when the original and conversion destination are on different drives. Because the process temporarily requires additional copies, both drives must have sufficient free space. Full conversion and returned-copy verification are required. **Important:** Swapping is not an atomic operation. If it's interrupted, successfully copied files are preserved rather than automatically removed. You may need to review the resulting folders manually. ### Customizing folders All folder settings are grouped under **Destination folders**: - **Converted Game Folder:** Where the new compressed game is initially saved. - **Original Game Folder:** Where the original is moved when using Move or Swap. - **Final Converted Game Folder:** Where the converted game is placed on the original drive when swapping. Only the folder options relevant to your selected operation are enabled. ## Compression settings The compressor uses **LZ4 HC** compression, with level **7** selected by default. LZ4 is designed for fast decompression, making it suitable for game assets that need to be accessed while playing. Actual storage savings depend on the game and its contents. Conversions use a multithreaded pipeline with a maximum of eight threads, including the coordinator. Most users can leave the default compression and verification settings unchanged. ## Canceling a conversion You can cancel a conversion while it's running. When canceling, the interface lets you choose whether to keep or delete the partially generated output. Keeping it may be useful for inspection, but an incomplete conversion should not be treated as a playable game. If a conversion fails, the compressor won't proceed with the selected move, delete, or swap operation on the original game. Failed or canceled jobs may still leave partial or completed folders behind. Check the locations reported by the interface before attempting another conversion. ## Things to know LZ4 Game Compressor is currently **beta software**. Although it includes storage checks and content verification, there are a few things worth keeping in mind: - **Compression results vary.** Games containing already-compressed assets may see smaller reductions in size. - **Verification isn't a compatibility test.** A verified conversion can still encounter issues when launching or playing. - **Keep a backup when possible.** Especially when trying a game for the first time. - **Deleting is permanent.** If you choose to remove your original, make sure you're comfortable relying on the converted copy. - **Interrupted operations may need cleanup.** In particular, moving or swapping games between drives can leave extra copies if the process doesn't finish. For the safest experience, start with **Keep both**, leave verification enabled, and test your compressed game before deleting the original. ## License and acknowledgments LZ4 Game Compressor is distributed under the **GPL-3.0-or-later** license. It incorporates licensed AMPR format, runtime, and packing code from [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu), along with third-party components including LZ4, PicoSHA2, nlohmann/json, and toml++. Additional information is available in: - [Credits and third-party acknowledgments](CREDITS.md) - [License](LICENSE) - [Source provenance](docs/PROVENANCE.md) - [Build instructions](docs/BUILD.md) When redistributing the application, preserve the applicable license notices and provide corresponding source code as required by the respective licenses. No game content or proprietary Sony SDK is included.

# LZ4 Compression for PS5

[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy_Me_a_Coffee-Support_this_project-FFDD00?style=for-the-badge&logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/theghostonline)

![LZ4 Compression](assets-app/pic0.png)

LZ4 compression for PS5 games, done entirely on the console. Pick a game,
choose `Compress with LZ4`, and it packs the game data into seekable LZ4 asset
packs that APR-EMU reads while the game runs, checks every file, and installs
the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime (adding it when the game ships none). The game
never has to leave the console.

It also does everything around that: `.ffpfsc` compression, exFAT/PFS images,
validate and repair, APR-EMU versions, copy and move, and a history of every
job.

Unofficial, and not affiliated with any of the projects it builds on. See
[Credits and license](#credits-and-license).

## The app

- **The PS5 app** (`LZ4 Compression`, title `PPSA99420`): a native app, no
  browser. Your library runs left to right like the home screen, every game
  opens its own page, and every action opens as a full page. D-pad and stick
  navigation with controller vibration, and Circle goes back.
- **The engine** (`lz4-compression.elf`): the payload that does the work. It
  serves the app and the web page on port `5920` and keeps its settings,
  caches and logs in `/data/LZ4Compression`. The app starts it through
  Payload Manager when it isn't running.
- **The web page** at `http://<PS5 IP>:5920` has the same features from a PC
  or phone, and it's where you upload TOML profiles from another device.
- It doesn't share a tile, port or settings folder with Game Compressor, so
  both can be installed.

## Install

1. Download `lz4-compression.elf` and `LZ4-Compression-PPSA99420.zip` from
   the [latest release](https://github.com/theghostonline/PS5-LZ4-Compression/releases/latest).
2. Add `lz4-compression.elf` to Payload Manager, so it sits at
   `/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf`. The app starts
   it from there.
3. Unzip the app and copy the `PPSA99420` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420`
   over FTP. ShadowMount+ adds the `LZ4 Compression` tile. It doesn't scan
   while a game is running, so close any game if the tile doesn't show up.
4. Open the tile. If the engine isn't running, the app starts it.

You can also skip the app: load the ELF and open `http://<PS5 IP>:5920` in
any browser.

## LZ4 asset packs

APR-EMU (drakmor's [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu)) can read
game data from seekable LZ4 asset packs while the game runs. LZ4 Compression
builds those packs for you:

1. Builds `ampr_emu.index` for the complete game.
2. Picks what to pack. The automatic profile scans the game: game data is
   packed, while executables, PRX/SPRX, `sce_sys`, `sce_module`, `fakelib`,
   saves, configs and already-compressed media stay loose. Large files that
   LZ4 can't shrink are sampled and left loose automatically.
3. Compresses every block with LZ4 at the level you pick (1 to 12) on all CPU cores.
4. Writes `ampr_assets.index`, its `.crc` and `.runtime` sidecars and the
   `ampr_assets-*.pak` volumes (AMPRPAK4 / AMPRDAT3, the same format
   `ampr_pack.py` writes).
5. Checks every packed file byte for byte against the original before
   anything is deleted.
6. Installs the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime (0.4.2.1 PackedStdio) into
   `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`.

### How to use it

LZ4 is the main action for every game that uses AMPR, which is most PS5
games, whether or not the dump ships APR-EMU. The app checks the game's
`eboot.bin` and `sce_module` for the `libSceAmpr` import. When the game has no
`fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`, packing adds the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime
there, and ShadowMount+ loads it in place of the system module when the game
starts. A game that never imports AMPR can't load APR-EMU, so it gets
`.ffpfsc` compression instead. Folder games work directly; `.exfat`, `.ffpfs`
and `.ffpfsc` images are mounted through ShadowMount+ for the job (close any
running game first, ShadowMount+ won't mount while one is open).

Open the game from the library: `Compress with LZ4` is its main button.
`.ffpfsc` Compress is under Options.

- **Compression level:** the same 1 to 12 scale as Lazy_AMPR. 1 to 4 use
  LZ4's fast mode, 5 to 12 use LZ4 HC. 9 is the default, 12 is the smallest
  and slowest.
- **Packing profile:** `Automatic` picks the best profile on its own. The
  app ships the tested community profiles from [`profiles/`](profiles/)
  (ASTRO BOT, EA Sports UFC 6, and the Insomniac and Unity engine profiles)
  and matches them by Title ID, by name, or by the game's file layout, so a
  matching game already has the right TOML when you open it. The game page
  shows which one it will use. Games without a match get the scan-based
  profile, and `Scan only` skips the bundled one.
- `Custom or Trace Config` uses your own
  `ampr_pack` TOML, for example one generated from APR traces with
  `ampr_pack_profile.py` or a community profile for the game. Two ways to get
  one in:
  - **Import config** in the PS5 app (or Import From Console on the web page)
    lists the `.toml` files in `/data/LZ4Compression/import` and on any USB
    drive (top folder, `toml`, `tomls`, `toml_profiles`, `profiles`,
    `LZ4Compression` or `Lazy_AMPR`). Files named after the Title ID or the
    game's name show up first, the same matching Lazy_AMPR uses.
    `include_from` lists next to the TOML are copied with it.
  - Upload `profile.toml` plus any `include_from` lists it names from a PC
    or phone browser.

  Your own config always wins over the bundled one. Profiles are stored in
  `/data/LZ4Compression/lz4-profiles/<TITLE_ID>/`, and the scan-based
  profile also learns the loose rules from every bundled and uploaded
  profile.
- **Destination:** next to the game, internal SSD or external storage. The
  output is a game folder named `<name>-lz4`.
- **Original handling:**
  - `Keep original` leaves the source alone.
  - `Delete after verified` removes it after the packs and every copied file
    were checked.
  - `Pack in place` (folders only) writes the packs inside the game folder,
    verifies them, then removes only the originals that are now inside the
    packs. It needs the least free space. If anything fails before the
    removal step, the folder, its `ampr_emu.index` and its APR-EMU file are
    put back exactly as they were.

LZ4 packed games show an `LZ4 Packed` chip, and their main action becomes
`Verify LZ4 Packs`, which decodes every block and checks it against the CRC
sidecar. `Uncompress LZ4` restores the loose game, either in place or as a new
folder.

While a game is LZ4 packed, `Build AMPR Index`, `Choose APR-EMU Version` and
`Restore Original APR-EMU` are blocked: the packs are tied to that exact
`ampr_emu.index`, and only the PackedStdio runtime can read them. The original
APR-EMU file is backed up first, so `Restore Original APR-EMU` is offered
again once you uncompress that folder in place. Compress to `.ffpfsc` and Make Image still work on a
packed folder and keep its index untouched.

### How it was checked

- The C packer was compared with drakmor's `ampr_pack.py` driven by
  Lazy_AMPR's own profile generator on the same files. File records, chunk
  records, pack volumes and CRC sidecars are byte-identical at LZ4 HC 9 and
  HC 12, with the automatic profile, a custom profile (streaming, striping,
  `store`, hash and round-robin lanes, group dedupe, volume rollover,
  `include_from`) and with learned loose patterns. Only the build ID differs.
  LZ4 fast output matches the official LZ4 1.10.0 library (`ampr_pack.py`
  with python-lz4 uses LZ4 1.9.4, which compresses fast mode differently).
- `ampr_pack.py verify --root`, `inspect` and `unpack` accept the packs built
  on the PS5.
- On a PS5 running firmware 13.60, packing, verifying, unpacking and in-place
  round trips through the app gave byte-identical results, on both
  internal storage and an exFAT M.2 drive.
- Packing straight from a ShadowMountPlus-mounted `.exfat` image on the PS5
  passed `ampr_pack.py verify --root` against the original files, and
  unpacking those packs gave back every file byte for byte. `.ffpfsc` sources
  use the same code path but haven't been tested on a console yet.

Results vary by game, and a trace-based profile is more reliable than the
automatic one. Keep a backup and launch the
game before you delete its original.

## Firmware 13.60 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7

Works with the current mount stack, so `Validate`, `Validate and Repair` and
`Update APR-EMU` work on current consoles:

- **Built with ps5-payload-sdk v0.43**, whose CRT supports firmware 13.60.
- **Accepts ShadowMountPlus 1.7's layered `mount_img.lnk` format.** SMP 1.7
  writes the link to the *outer* container (`layers=2`, e.g.
  `/data/homebrew/GAME.ffpfsc`) instead of the 1.6-style nested path
  (`/mnt/shadowmnt/pfsc/<name>/GAME.exfat`). The remount verification now
  derives the expected nested directory from the actual link and accepts the
  layered form, so compressed `.ffpfsc` titles pass the mount gate again.
- **Accepts folder titles exposed as real files on `/system_ex`** (firmware
  13.60 behavior with kstuff 1.11), not only `nullfs` overlays, in the
  `system_ex` binding check used by `Update APR-EMU` and mount verification.
- **Self-healing mounts:** SMP keeps its LVD image mounts across
  restarts while LZ4 Compression clears mount links at the start of
  mount-dependent operations, which could previously leave both sides waiting
  on each other. While waiting for a remount, LZ4 Compression now asks SMP's
  local API to mount the title (`POST 127.0.0.1:10101/api/v1/games/mount`)
  after 5 s and every 15 s afterwards, so `Validate`, `Validate and Repair`,
  and compress finalize recover on their own. The nudge is a best-effort
  hint: if SMP's API is disabled the wait falls back to the previous
  scan/restart behavior.

Tested on PS5 firmware **13.60** with **kstuff-lite 1.11** and
**ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta3/1.7beta4**: a 67 GB title compressed to `.ffpfsc`
(19.5 GB) and its full hash validation (1,029,215 blocks) completed clean,
with the title mounted and launchable afterwards.

## Rest mode and interrupted jobs

During ordinary copying, compression, unpacking, scanning, and validation,
LZ4 Compression allows automatic rest mode. If the PS5 preserves the payload
process, the worker continues after wake and the web UI refreshes its progress
and history when reopened. During source deletion, destructive stream
compression, block repair, and mount/configuration changes, LZ4 Compression
renews the console's automatic rest timer until the critical phase ends.

The power timer cannot prevent someone from choosing rest mode manually.
Avoid manual rest while an operation is changing existing game data. If the
payload stops during rest or restarts afterward, unfinished jobs are recorded
as interrupted in history. Queued jobs are cancelled, and running jobs are
marked failed; neither is restarted automatically. Inspect the source and
output paths before retrying, especially after destructive compression or
deletion.

## Main Features

- Compress mounted game folders or images into FF-PFSC output.
- Choose PFS or exFAT output when compressing.
- Automatically build APR Emu `ampr_emu.index` before compressing APR titles.
- Manually run `Build AMPR Index` on a folder when you only want to refresh the
  APR index.
- Compress games into seekable LZ4 asset packs on the PS5, verify
  them, and uncompress them again (see above).
- Validate compressed games and repair detected PFSC block issues when possible.
- Uncompress compressed games back to folder/app form.
- Move supported titles between internal storage and USB storage.
- Track progress, speed, estimated remaining time, and operation history.
- Keep operations running on the PS5 even if the app or the browser tab
  closes.

## APR Emu Support

APR Emu titles need an `ampr_emu.index` file and the correct ShadowMountPlus
read-only image settings when they are run from internal SSD. LZ4 Compression
handles those details for the common workflows:

- To compress a folder-format APR Emu game from USB and run it from internal
  SSD, plug in the USB drive, select the title, and choose `Compress`. The
  app builds `ampr_emu.index` using the same workflow as
  `build_ampr_index.py`, writes the ShadowMountPlus read-only and sector-size
  settings, creates the `.ffpfsc` image, mounts it, and validates the mounted
  image byte-for-byte against the original.
- If the compressed game stutters and you still want it on internal SSD, open
  the game page and choose `Uncompress` under Options, then select `exFAT`. The
  ShadowMountPlus settings and `ampr_emu.index` are already in place, so the
  app leaves them unchanged and creates an uncompressed exFAT image.
- If you already know the game should stay uncompressed, choose `Make Image`
  under Options, then select `exFAT` and `Internal SSD`.
  LZ4 Compression detects the APR Emu title, builds or refreshes
  `ampr_emu.index`, applies the read-only ShadowMountPlus settings, and creates
  the uncompressed image.
- If you already have an exFAT image and `ampr_emu.index` exists, use `Set Read
  Only` under Options to apply the ShadowMountPlus read-only
  settings for that image.

The only unsupported automatic case is an existing exFAT image with no
`ampr_emu.index`. For that case, run the game once from external USB without
read-only settings so APR Emu can create its index, confirm the game starts,
then copy it to internal SSD and use `Set Read Only`.

Non-APR titles keep the normal compression path. When APR indexing is performed,
the selected game screen and operation history show `APR indexed`.

The in-app `APR-EMU Version` picker uses Pippo's public APR-EMU manifest and
binary mirror:

```text
https://pippo26442999.github.io/.exFAT/ampr-emu-drakmor/manifest.json
```

The manifest and hosted files are provided by Pippo (`pippo26442999`). Manifest
entries are downloaded by the browser, uploaded to LZ4 Compression, cached under
`/data/LZ4Compression/ampr-emu`, and then applied to the selected title or
image. Custom `.sprx`/`.prx` files can also be uploaded manually from a desktop
browser. The upstream APR Emu project source is
[drakmor/ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu).

## Requirements

- A PS5 homebrew environment capable of running payload ELFs.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) latest version,
  installed and managing mounted titles.
- [KStuff Lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite/releases/tag/v1.07)
  1.07 Beta or later.
- [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) or another
  method to launch `lz4-compression.elf`.

This project assumes you already understand the risks of running PS5 homebrew
payloads. Keep backups of important data and test with non-critical titles
first.

## Build

For firmware 13.60, use [ps5-payload-sdk v0.43](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/tag/v0.43)
or newer. Its CRT contains the 13.60 kernel initialization case. Earlier
builds can fail before `main()` and create no application log.
The build checks the SDK CRT for that case and refuses an unsupported SDK.

On Linux or WSL, install `make`, Python 3, Clang 18, and LLD 18. Set
`PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` to the extracted SDK path, then run `make`:

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
make
```

The needed zlib 1.3.1 sources are included under `third_party/zlib` and are
built for PS5 along with the payload. No external zlib path is required.

The build output is:

```text
lz4-compression.elf
```

The 13.60 build has been checked for successful compilation and ELF format.
A locally built payload was also launched successfully on a PS5 running
firmware 13.60.

GitHub Actions builds the ELF on pushes and pull requests. Pushing a `v*` tag
also creates or updates a GitHub Release containing `lz4-compression.elf` and
`SHA256SUMS`. The workflow downloads the pinned SDK v0.43 release, verifies its
SHA-256 checksum, and checks that its CRT contains the firmware 13.60 case.

LZ4 1.10.0 (`third_party/lz4`) and the pinned APR-EMU PackedStdio runtime
(`third_party/ampr_emu`, SHA-256 checked at build time) are included too.

The LZ4 packer also builds on a PC so it can be checked against
`ampr_pack.py`:

```sh
make -f tests/host/Makefile
build/host/ampr_pack_cli pack <game folder> <output folder> --embedded-runtime
python ampr_pack.py verify --index <output folder>/ampr_assets.index --root <game folder>
```

`tests/ps5/Makefile` builds `lz4-selftest.elf`, which packs, verifies,
unpacks and round-trips `/data/lz4test/game` on the console and writes
`/data/lz4test/selftest.log`.

`tests/ui/run.sh` checks the web UI on a PC: it starts a stub of the payload
API and drives the page in Playwright's WebKit (library, game pages, LZ4 and
compress pages, back navigation, splash and done screens, phone width). It
needs Pillow and Playwright (`pip install pillow playwright` and
`playwright install webkit`).

Generated build outputs are intentionally ignored by git:

```text
build/
gen/
lz4-compression.elf
```

## The PS5 app

`app/lz4-compression` is the console app (title `PPSA99420`): the library,
game pages and action pages with D-pad and stick navigation, controller
vibration and no browser. It talks to the engine (`lz4-compression.elf`) on
`127.0.0.1:5920` and starts it through Payload Manager when it isn't running.
The web page on port 5920 stays available from a PC or phone, for example to
upload LZ4 profiles.

It is built with [PS5 React](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react) on macOS
(Apple Silicon):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/half144/ps5-react.git && cd ps5-react
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && npm ci
brew install cmake sdl2 llvm@18 curl libarchive
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" npm run dev -- --app-dir ../PS5-LZ4-Compression/app/lz4-compression    # desktop preview
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" npm run build -- --app-dir ../PS5-LZ4-Compression/app/lz4-compression  # dist/PPSA99420
```

Keep LLVM 18 out of `PATH` (the build finds it on its own); the host tools
need Apple's clang. Copy `dist/PPSA99420` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420` and
ShadowMount+ adds the tile.

## Deploy

Copy the built ELF to your PS5 payload folder. A typical Payload Manager path is:

```text
/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf
```

This repo also includes Payload Manager metadata in:

```text
payload-manager/lz4-compression.elf.json
```

Fill in its `checksum` with the SHA-256 of the ELF you publish (each build
has its own linker build ID, so every build has a different hash; release
builds list theirs in the release's `SHA256SUMS`).

## How To Use

1. Make sure ShadowMountPlus has mounted one or more games.
2. Open the `LZ4 Compression` tile, or load `lz4-compression.elf` and open
   `http://<PS5_IP>:5920/` in a browser.
3. Move along the library row and open a game.
4. Use the main button on the game page:
   - Games that use AMPR show `Compress with LZ4`.
   - Other folder and image games show `Compress` (`.ffpfsc`).
   - Compressed games show `Validate and Repair`.
   - LZ4 packed games show `Verify LZ4 Packs`.
5. Everything else is on the same page under Options, grouped as Compress,
   Check, Restore, APR-EMU, Copy and move, and Delete.
6. Use the History button in the top bar to review previous operations. The
   home screen also shows the most recent ones.

Jobs run in the engine, so they keep going if you close the app or the
browser. Open either again to see the current job. When you're done, use the
power button in the top bar to stop the engine before you play.

## Compression Settings

When you choose `Compress`, LZ4 Compression asks for the output format,
destination, and how to handle the original source.

### Format

`Compress` always produces a `.ffpfsc` file, which is a compressed PFS container.
The format choice controls the nested image stored inside that compressed
container:

- `exFAT` is the default and recommended nested image format. It stores an exFAT
  image inside the `.ffpfsc` output and is the preferred option for most games,
  especially APR Emu workflows.
- `PFS Experimental` stores a PFS image inside the `.ffpfsc` output. Use it only
  when you specifically want to test the PFS nested-image path.

### Destination

- `Compress in place` writes the compressed `.ffpfsc` container next to the
  currently selected game.
- `Internal SSD` writes the compressed output under `/data/homebrew`. This is
  only shown when the selected game is not already on internal storage.
- `External Storage` writes the compressed output to a selected USB/external
  target. If the game is already on external storage, LZ4 Compression may show a
  `Compress to...` picker so you can choose internal SSD or another USB target.

### Original Handling

- `Keep original` leaves the source folder or image untouched. This is the
  safest choice and requires enough free space for the compressed output.
- `Delete after verified` writes and validates the compressed output first, then
  removes the original source. This is the default for in-place compression. It
  still needs full-size temporary free space because the original is kept until
  verification succeeds.
- `Destructive` deletes source data while writing the compressed output. It
  requires at least 1 GB of free space, cannot be cancelled after the unsafe
  phase begins, and is only available for same-storage folder compression. It is
  not available when compressing to another drive or when using `Make Image`.

When compressing to internal SSD or external storage, LZ4 Compression keeps the
original by default. If you choose to remove the original, it uses the safer
`Delete after verified` behavior.

## Game Discovery

The library only lists games. Apps that ShadowMount+ mounts next to them
(homebrew, media apps) are left out: anything under 2 GB once its size is
known counts as an app.

Mounted games are shown automatically. LZ4 Compression also scans known game
storage folders, including:

```text
/data/homebrew
/data/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext0
/mnt/ext0/homebrew
/mnt/ext0/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext1
/mnt/ext1/homebrew
/mnt/ext1/etaHEN/games
/mnt/usb0 through /mnt/usb7
/mnt/usb0/homebrew through /mnt/usb7/homebrew
/mnt/usb0/etaHEN/games through /mnt/usb7/etaHEN/games
```

## When You Are Done

Only run LZ4 Compression while you need to compress, validate, repair, move or
unpack games. Once you're done, close it so it doesn't take anything away from
your games.

In the app, use the power button in the top bar and pick `Stop engine and
close`. The engine stops and the app closes, and the tile stays on the home
screen for next time. On the web page the power button stops the engine and
shows a closing screen.

## Notes

- Payload operations are owned by the PS5-side engine, not the app or the
  browser tab.
- Compression and repair workflows can take a long time on large titles.

## Support

LZ4 Compression was built and tested on a real console, one game, pack and
firmware quirk at a time. Donations here go to this project, not to the
projects it builds on (see the credits below). If it saved you space on your
PS5, a coffee helps cover the cost of building it and keeps the updates coming.

<a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/theghostonline"><img src="https://cdn.buymeacoffee.com/buttons/v2/default-yellow.png" alt="Buy Me a Coffee" height="50"></a>

Not able to donate? A star on the repository and a bug report with the game,
title ID and firmware help just as much.

## Credits and license

LZ4 Compression is built on [PS5 Game Compressor](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-Game-Compressor)
by Juma Sayeh, with firmware 13.60 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 support by gcoding97

by Drakmor's [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu). Third-party
components and their licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; original
copyright notices are kept in the source files.

## Disclaimer

This is homebrew software for experimental PS5 workflows. Use it at your own
risk. The project is not affiliated with Sony, PlayStation, or any game
publisher. To be used with own game dumps.

latestRelease.body:
# LZ4 Compression 1.3.0

The first release of LZ4 Compression: LZ4 packs for PS5 games, made right on
the console.

## LZ4 asset packs

- `Compress with LZ4` packs game data into seekable LZ4 packs that APR-EMU
  reads while the game runs. Executables, system files and already-compressed
  media stay loose.
- Works on any game that uses AMPR, not just the ones that ship APR-EMU. The
  app checks the game's `eboot.bin` and `sce_module` for `libSceAmpr`, and
  when there's no `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx` it adds the pack-capable APR-EMU
  runtime for you. Games that don't use AMPR get `.ffpfsc` compression
  instead.
- Compression level from 1 to 12, the same scale as Lazy_AMPR. 1 to 4 use
  LZ4's fast mode, 5 to 12 use LZ4 HC, and 9 is the default.
- Automatic profile, or your own `ampr_pack` TOML. `Import config` finds
  TOMLs on a USB drive or in `/data/LZ4Compression/import` and puts the ones
  named after the game first. You can also upload them from a PC or phone.
- Works on game folders and on `.exfat` and `.ffpfs` images. ShadowMount+
  only mounts images while a game runs, so the app mounts them itself for the
  job.
- Write the packed game next to the original, to the internal SSD or to
  external storage, or pack a folder in place to use the least free space.
- Every packed file is compared byte for byte with the original before
  anything is removed.
- `Verify LZ4 Packs` checks every block, and `Uncompress LZ4` gives you back
  the normal loose game.

## The app

- A native PS5 app (`PPSA99420`), no browser. D-pad and stick navigation,
  controller vibration, and Circle goes back.
- Your games run left to right like the home screen, every game opens its
  own page, and every action opens as a full page.
- The engine (`lz4-compression.elf`) does the work, and the app starts it
  through Payload Manager when it isn't running. The web page on port 5920
  is still there for a PC or phone.

It also does `.ffpfsc` compression and uncompression, exFAT/PFS images,
validate and repair, APR-EMU versions, and copy and move.

## Install

1. Add `lz4-compression.elf` to Payload Manager, so it sits at
   `/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf`.
2. Unzip `LZ4-Compression-PPSA99420.zip` and copy the `PPSA99420` folder to
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420` over FTP. ShadowMount+ adds the
   `LZ4 Compression` tile (close any running game if it doesn't show up).
3. Open the tile.

Tested on firmware 13.60 with Payload Manager, kstuff and ShadowMount+ 1.7.
It has its own tile, port (`5920`) and settings folder
(`/data/LZ4Compression`), so it can be installed next to Game Compressor.

Keep your original game until you've launched the packed version.
